sentences.text: FACTUAL BACKGROUND 2.

It is averred in the plaint that, in the month of March 2022, the defendant who is relative of plaintiff approached the plaintiff with a proposal that, he is having a property bearing No. WZ-18,
Second Floor, Back side, Budhela, Vikaspuri, New Delhi, measuring 94 Sq. Yards and wishes to sell out the said property as he was in dire need of money.

It is further averred that, after discussion, the cost of the aforesaid property was fixed at Rs.17,00,000/- and on 03.04.2022 the plaintiff paid to the defendant bayana amount of Rs.4,00,000/- vide a cheque bearing No. 671629 drawn on State Bank of India dated 04.04.2022 which was duly encashed by the defendant in his account.

It is further averred that, when the plaintiff asked the defendant to execute the Bayana Agreement on multiple occasions, the defendant avoided the plaintiff on one reason or the other and did not execute the Agreement for sale and purchase of his aforesaid property in the name of the plaintiff for a long period.

3. It is further averred that, being suspicious, plaintiff enquired about the property and came to know that the aforesaid property do not belongs to the defendant and belongs to Prosper SHILPI M JAIN Digitally signed CS No. 135/25 ORS. Vs. BHAGWAN DASS.

It is further averred that, when plaintiff questioned the defendant about the above fact, the defendant agreed to return the aforesaid bayana amount to the plaintiff and in discharge of his legal debt/liability, the defendant issued a Post Dated cheque in favour of the plaintiff i.e. cheque bearing No. 114731 dated 03.06.2023 for Rs.4,00,000/-, drawn on Bank of India, Vikaspuri, New Delhi-110018 with assurance that it would be honoured on presentation but when the plaintiff presented the aforesaid cheque for encashment with his banker i.e. State Bank of India, Dwarka District Court Complex, Sector-10, Dwarka, New Delhi it returned unpaid with the remarks "Funds Insufficient" vide returning memo dated 07.06.2023.

It is further averred that, on assurance of defendant, plaintiff again presented the said cheque for encashment but it was again returned unpaid with the same remarks ie "Funds Insufficient"
vide returning memo dated 28.08.2023.

It is further averred that, due to this reason plaintiff's wife suffered brain hemorrhage and was hospitalized and remain on Ventilator for about 29 days and at last despite of his best efforts, the plaintiff could not able to save his wife.
It is further averred that, on being asked about the the payment and dishonor of cheque, defendant always gave false assurances to SHILPI M JAIN by SHILPI M CS No. 135/25 ORS. Vs. BHAGWAN DASS.

sentences.text: 16:59:59 +0530 8. PW1 in his examination-in-chief through affidavit Ex.PW1/1 has deposed the facts as narrated in the plaint mentioned above.

He inter-alia proved the Copy of the Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/1 (OSR),
Original Bank statement/transaction as Ex.PW1/2, Certified copy of the cheques of defendant as Ex.PW1/3, Certificate copy of the cheque returning memo dated 07.06.2023 as Ex.PW1/4,

There is no cross-examination of any of PW1.
9.
The entire verbal testimony as well as the documentary evidence adduced on record has gone unchallenged and uncontroverted as defendant remained ex-parte.

On careful reading of the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Basalingappa v. Mudibasappa1, makes it clear that the presumption under Section 139 of the N.I Act provides that Court shall presume that the holder of a cheque received the cheque for the discharge, in whole or in part of any debt or other liability.
The burden lies on the issuer to rebut the presumption.
The probable defence raised by the defendant/issuer would be a matter to be decided on the facts of each case and the circumstances that existed.
But, defendant chosen to remain absent.

11. In view of the foregoing discussions, the suit of the plaintiff is allowed.

The plaintiff is held entitled to a money decree of Rs. 4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakh Only) along with interest @ 6% p.a.
on decretal amount from the date of institution of the suit till the realization of the amount against the defendant.

12. Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
